findings.issue: The Stop-gate opt-in is written only by ApplyHookInstall after the conflict check, so in a repo with a foreign core.hooksPath (husky, lefthook, beads) or active .git/hooks an unforced install refuses and the opt-in is never recorded; setup --check's remediation points at that same refusing command.
findings.consequence: Repos with other hook managers (incl. this clone, core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks) were gated before #194 and are now silently ungated; the only ways back are --force (clobbers their hooks) or an undocumented manual git config.

findings.issue: The hook exits 0 silently when the key is not 'true', without distinguishing a repo that never opted in from one whose metareview git gate is installed but whose opt-in is missing (upgraded pre-#194 install, or an agent running `git config --unset metareview.stopGate`).
findings.consequence: An agent can silently disable its own turn-end gate, and upgraded installs silently lose the Stop gate — contradicting the script's own 'stand down loudly' rule.

findings.issue: session-start-check.sh checks only core.hooksPath and never the Stop-gate opt-in, so an upgraded 0.13.x install is never told its Stop gate went inert.
findings.consequence: Repos lose the Stop gate on upgrade with nothing in the session saying so.

findings.issue: withStopGateOptIn keeps enforcement.active true for a repo that has not opted in; the amended AC says setup --check reports the Stop gate as inactive there.
findings.consequence: Consumers of enforcement.active see an active gate where it does nothing.

findings.issue: Nothing ties the Go StopGateKey to the key hard-coded in hooks/pre-finish.sh; a StopGateKey typo survives every test (mutation-verified).
findings.consequence: Key drift makes install report success while the hook stays inert everywhere, with CI green.

findings.issue: The Check() wiring of withStopGateOptIn is untested (removing it survives).
findings.consequence: The optedIn upgrade signal the docs rely on could vanish with no test failing.

Therefore repositories that cannot proceed with hook installation cannot opt into the independently registered Stop hook through this workflow. The comment explicitly identifies pre-#194 installs as needing migration, yet the migration path does not cover conflicting hook configurations. Claims about the exact check remediation and this particular clone are not shown, but the core compatibility and migration defect is directly supported by the diff.

output.summary: Husky-case guidance names --enable-stop-gate; new suite in run-all.

findings.issue: The --enable-stop-gate hint fires for any non-empty core.hooksPath that is not the fully materialized target, including metareview's own paths that PlanHookInstall does not treat as conflicts (isOurHookPath): the legacy hooks/git install, and .metareview/git-hooks with deleted scripts. The notice then claims the path is set by another tool and install will refuse.
findings.consequence: On a legacy upgrade or vanished git-ignored scripts, the agent is steered to the Stop-gate-only opt-in and the push gate a plain --install-hooks would restore stays uninstalled (reproduced).
